```{r running INLA models with jrbp data}

### setting desired species and U values
species_options <- c("CASJ","SPTO","CBCH","BEWR","RTHA")
u_values <- c(0.005,0.0075,0.01,0.015,0.02,0.025,0.03)

### initialization
data <- list()
species_data <- list()

### determining distribution according to species
distribution_function <- function(species){
  if (species == "RTHA"){x = "poisson"}
  else x = "nbinomial"
  return(x)
}

### running and saving INLA models

for (i in 1:length(species_options)){
  for (j in 1:length(u_values)){
    species <- species_options[i]
    U <- u_values[j]
    distribution <- distribution_function(species_options[i])

    speciescol <- paste0('n.',species)
    MyData <- na.exclude(df[, c(speciescol,
                            "Census_Area", "Day_of_year", "Date", 'Year',
                            'ID',
                            "Observer1")])
    names(MyData)[1] <- 'Abundance'
    bspecies <- MyData[,1]

    hyper.prec <- list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(U, 0.05)))
    inla.setOption(scale.model.default = TRUE)

    I1 <- inla(Abundance ~ f(Year, model = "rw1", hyper = hyper.prec) + 
             f(Day_of_year, model = "rw2", hyper = hyper.prec) +
             f(Census_Area, model = "iid") +
             f(Observer1, model = "iid"),
           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, 
                                    quantiles = c("0.025", "0.975")),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE,
                                  waic = TRUE),
           family = distribution,
           data = MyData)
    
    MyData$Fitted <- I1$summary.fitted.values[,'mean']
    
    Yearsm <- I1$summary.random$Year
    
    model <- data.frame(species = species_options[i],
                        U = u_values[j],
                        ID = Yearsm$ID,
                        mean = Yearsm$mean,
                        quant1 = Yearsm$`0.025quant`,
                        quant2 = Yearsm$`0.975quant`)
    
    species_data[[j]] <- model
  }
  data[[i]] <- species_data
}

bound_data <- bind_rows(data)

```

```{r plotting jrbp INLA models}

ggplot(bound_data,
       aes(x = ID)) + 
  xlab("Year") + ylab("Trend") + 
  geom_line(data = bound_data,
            aes(y = mean)) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymax = quant1, 
                  ymin = quant2), 
              alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,
             linetype = "dashed") + 
  facet_grid(species ~ U) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8,
                                   angle = 45),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
        ) + 
  ggtitle('Trend by Year') + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 15, 
                                  lineheight = .8, 
                                  face = "bold", 
                                  hjust = 0.5)) + 
  ylim(min(bound_data$quant1 - 0.05),
       max(bound_data$quant2) + 0.05)



```

```{r running INLA models with ccber data}

### setting desired NCOS species

species_options <- c("Killdeer","Common Yellowthroat","American Crow","Song Sparrow","Northern Shoveler","Least Sandpiper","Gadwall","Semipalmated Plover","Red-shouldered Hawk")


### initialization

yearsm_list <- list()
dayY_list <- list()
myData_list <- list()
magdf_list <- list()
E1_list <- list()
dispersion_list <- list()
DIC_list <- list()
variogram1_list <- list()
variogram2_list <- list()
year_marg_list <- list()
percent_change_list <- list()
percent_change_intervals_list <- list()

breaks <- seq(0.5, 20.5, length = 20)
breaks2 <- seq(0.5, 364.5, length = 365)


### running and saving INLA models with a default of U = 0.05

for (i in 1:length(species_options)){
  
  ### INLA model
  
    species <- species_options[i]
    U <- 0.05
    distribution <- "poisson"

    speciescol <- species
    MyData <- na.exclude(data[, c(speciescol,
                                  "day_of_survey_year",
                                  "observation_date",
                                  'year',
                                  'survey_id')])
    names(MyData)[1] <- 'Abundance'
    bspecies <- MyData[,1]

    hyper.prec <- list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(U, 0.05)))
    inla.setOption(scale.model.default = TRUE)

    I1 <- inla(Abundance ~ f(year, model = "rw1", hyper = hyper.prec) + 
             f(day_of_survey_year, model = "rw2", hyper = hyper.prec),
           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, 
                                    quantiles = c("0.025", "0.975")),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE,
                                  waic = TRUE),
           family = distribution,
           data = MyData)
    
  ### calculations and saving data
    
    MyData$Fitted <- I1$summary.fitted.values[,'mean']
    
    # trend for year
    Yearsm <- I1$summary.random$year
    
    # calculating residuals
    mu <- MyData$Fitted
    theta <- I1$summary.hyperpar[1, "mean"]
    
    if(distribution == 'nbinomial'){
      # Pearson residuals for negative binomial distribution
      E1 <- (bspecies - mu) / sqrt(mu + mu^2 / theta) 
    }
    if(distribution == 'poisson'){
      # Pearson residuals for poisson distribution
      E1 <- (bspecies - mu) / sqrt(mu) 
    }
    if(distribution == 'gaussian'){
      # Residuals for gaussian distribution
      E1 <-  MyData$Abundance-MyData$Fitted
    }
    names(E1)[1] <- "Residuals"
    
    
    ### Check for overdispersion
    
    N <- nrow(MyData)
    p <- nrow(I1$summary.fixed)
    Dispersion <- sum(E1^2) / (N - p)
    
    
    ### Day of Year Trends
    
    DayY <- I1$summary.random$Day_of_year
    MyData$Residuals <- E1$Residuals
    
    
    ### variograms
    
    # Variogram for checking for temporal autocorrelation by year 
    MyData$E1 <- E1
    MyData$Zeros <- rep(0, nrow(MyData))
    V1 <- variog(coords = MyData[, c("Year", "Zeros")], data = MyData$E1, breaks = breaks)
    
    # Variogram for checking for temporal autocorrelation by data of year
    V2 <- variog(coords = MyData[, c("Day_of_year", "Zeros")], data = MyData$E1, breaks = breaks2)
    
    
    ### Extract the posterior marginal distributions for Year random walk
    year.marg <- I1$marginals.random$Year 
    
    
    ### Create dataframe for storing data
    Magdf <- data.frame(Year = seq(from = 1989, to = 2020, by = 1))
    for(i in 1:32) { 
      # Transform the posterior marginal distribution for current year so that it is not in log scale
      tmarg <- inla.tmarginal(exp, year.marg[[i]]) 
      # Calculate mean value for year i
      Magdf$mean[i] <- mean(tmarg[,1]) 
      # Calculate 95% CRI for year i's estimate
      Magdf$cri95[i] <- mean(inla.qmarginal(0.5, tmarg) - inla.qmarginal(0.025, tmarg), 
                             inla.qmarginal(0.975, tmarg) - inla.qmarginal(0.5, tmarg))
      # Calculate mean percent change current year vs initial
      Magdf$percent.change.mean[i] <- 100 * (Magdf$mean[i] - Magdf$mean[1]) / Magdf$mean[1] 
      # Calculate variance in percent change using 95% CRIs and variance estimation method 
      Magdf$percent.change.cri95[i] <- Magdf$mean[i] / Magdf$mean[1] *
        sqrt((Magdf$cri95[i]^2 / Magdf$mean[i]^2) + (Magdf$cri95[1]^2 / Magdf$mean[1]^2)) * 100
      Magdf$lower.cri95[i] <- Magdf$percent.change.mean[i] - (Magdf$percent.change.cri95[i])
      Magdf$upper.cri95[i] <- Magdf$percent.change.mean[i] + (Magdf$percent.change.cri95[i])
    }
    
    
    ### saving data
    
    yearsm_individual <- data.frame(species = species_options[i],
                                    ID = Yearsm$ID,
                                    mean = Yearsm$mean,
                                    quant0.025 = Yearsm$`0.025quant`,
                                    quant0.975 = Yearsm$`0.975quant`)
    
    dayY_individual <- data.frame(species = species_options[i],
                                  ID = DayY$ID,
                                  mean = DayY$mean,
                                  quant0.025 = DayY$`0.025quant`,
                                  quant0.975 = DayY$`0.975quant`)
    
    myData_individual <- data.frame(species = species_options[i],
                                    abundance = MyData$Abundance,
                                    day_of_year = MyData$Day_of_year,
                                    date = MyData$Date,
                                    year = MyData$Year,
                                    fitted = MyData$Fitted,
                                    residuals = MyData$Residuals,
                                    E1 = MyData$E1)
    
    magdf_individual <- data.frame(species = species_options[i],
                                   year = Magdf$Year,
                                   change = Magdf$percent.change.mean,
                                   lower = Magdf$lower.cri95,
                                   upper = Magdf$upper.cri95)
    
  # data frames
  yearsm_list[[i]] <- yearsm_individual
  dayY_list[[i]] <- dayY_individual
  myData_list[[i]] <- myData_individual
  magdf_list[[i]] <- magdf_individual
  
  # model residuals
  E1_list[[i]] <- E1$Residuals
  
  # dispersion and dic
  dispersion_list[[i]] <- Dispersion
  DIC_list[[i]] <- I1$dic$dic
  
  # variogram data
  variogram1_list[[i]] <- V1
  variogram2_list[[i]] <- V2
  
  # posterior marginal distribution for year random walk
  year_marg_list[[i]] <- year.marg[[32]]
  
  # percent change since survey start mean and 95% confidence interval
  percent_change_list[[i]] <- Magdf$percent.change.mean[32]
  percent_change_intervals_list[[i]] <- Magdf$percent.change.cri95[32]
  
}

```

# looking for residual patterns

# Variogram for checking for temporal autocorrelation by year 
# nearly flat line near 1 indicates low autocorrelation
plot(V1, type = "b", 
     xlab = "Time difference (years)", ylab = "Sample Variogram",
     col = 1, pch = 16, cex = 1.5)

# Variogram for checking for temporal autocorrelation by data of year
plot(V1, type = "b", 
     xlab = "Time difference (day of year)", ylab = "Sample Variogram",
     col = 1, pch = 16, cex = 1.5, ylim = c(0,2))

# Plot Residuals vs. fitted values and covariates
plot(E1$Residuals ~ MyData$Fitted) # Residuals vs fitted values
# looking for adherence to 0 line with minor variability
qqPlot(E1$Residuals)
# looking for points within theoretical line bounds
# determines whether or not residuals are distributed normally
hist(E1$Residuals) # histogram of residuals
plot(E1$Residuals ~ MyData$Abundance, data = MyData) 
plot(MyData$Fitted ~ MyData$Abundance, asp= 1, data = MyData)
plot(MyData$Fitted ~ MyData$Abundance, data = MyData)

plot(E1$Residuals ~ Year, data = MyData)
plot(E1$Residuals ~ Day_of_year, data = MyData)
